_comment: Round 61 (R252): how every SDK's feed follower keeps the feed head. Each case is a run of the follower over pages served in order. A page has the event sequences it carries, its next_after and the head it ends with (null for none). handle_until is the last event the caller finishes before it stops following (null: it finishes every event). A head is kept only when its sequence equals its page's next_after and only after the caller finished every event on that page; a newer kept head is reported once; the same head statement (the same statement label, standing for the same head_statement_hash) is not reported again, while a fresh statement for the same sequence (the server makes one after its 5-minute reuse ends, with a later time) replaces the kept one and is reported; a lower or non-matching head is never kept. expected_kept is the head ({sequence, statement}) the caller can read at the end (null for none); expected_reported lists the heads reported to the caller, in order. The Go SDK (FollowSignalsOptions.OnHead, FollowSignalsError.Head) set this rule; every SDK and this file must agree. Each head is {sequence, statement}: statement is a label for the head's head_statement_hash; a test serves a head whose head_statement_hash is derived from the label (for example its SHA-256), so equal labels mean the same statement. Each event's event_hash is derived from its sequence (for example the SHA-256 of "e" followed by the sequence), and a head's head_hash is the event_hash of the event at its sequence unless the head names head_hash_of, the sequence whose event_hash it carries instead; a head is kept only when its head_hash equals the event_hash of the last event the caller finished (round 61: both reports proposed it, and the verifier already fails such a head). A case may name start: {after, after_hash_of}: the follower starts after that event, and when after_hash_of is given the caller passes the event_hash of event after_hash_of as the hash of the event it last finished (a follower resuming at the feed's end keeps the head it is served); with start null the follower starts at 0 having finished no event.

cases.name: a head matching a finished page is kept and reported
a page without a head keeps nothing
a head that does not match the page's next_after is not kept
a head on a page the caller did not finish is not kept
the same head on idle polls is reported once
a newer head replaces the kept one and is reported
a lower head never replaces the kept one
a page that is not the end carries no head, and the head at the end is kept
a fresh statement for the same sequence replaces the kept one and is reported
a head naming another event's hash is not kept
a head with the right hash but another sequence is not kept
a follower resuming at the end with the hash of its last event keeps the head
a follower resuming at the end without that hash keeps no head
